response: {"hypotheses":[{"title":"Boundary sentinels with failure-contingent escalation","claim":"Appending exactly this one system-prompt instruction—\"For multi-module Python changes, spend verification first on the fastest discriminating check for each impacted module boundary, expand testing around a boundary only when its sentinel fails or reveals uncertainty, and preserve enough time to finalize before the deadline.\"—will, compared with no appended instruction under the same agent, tasks, tools, and deadline, lower regression_count without increasing deadline misses; pass_rate, tool_calls, wall_time, and cost are outcomes to measure, not assumed benefits.","rationale":"The named causal mechanism is failure-contingent sequential testing: a cheap sentinel buys broad boundary coverage early, while adaptive escalation concentrates additional effort only where observed failure or ambiguity raises posterior defect risk. This can avoid exhaustive low-yield checks while still probing interactions across modules. Test it with a preregistered paired A/B benchmark of hidden multi-module Python tasks, multiple seeds, identical overall budgets, trace-based coding of sentinel and escalation choices, and explicit non-inferiority tests for pass_rate and deadline misses.","assumptions":["The agent can identify impacted module boundaries from the patch and repository structure.","At least one fast, discriminating verification action exists for most impacted boundaries.","Sentinel outcomes provide useful evidence about where broader verification is warranted.","The benchmark separately captures regressions, correct completion, deadline misses, tool calls, wall time, and cost."],"risks":["A passing sentinel may provide false reassurance and suppress broader tests that would expose a latent interaction defect.","The agent may choose weak sentinels that merely recheck implementation details rather than observable behavior.","Many impacted boundaries can make even one check per boundary too slow and increase deadline misses.","Failure-triggered escalation can thrash on noisy or flaky tests and consume the finalization reserve.","Single-module, configuration, packaging, or end-to-end failures may receive too little attention.","Visible benchmark structure may encourage sentinel selection that games benchmark-specific patterns."]}]}
